newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks seen hovering in narrow range.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks seen hovering in narrow range.

text.p: Tokyo stocks are likely to hover narrowly on Wednesday, as expected gains in blue-chip exporters triggered by the yen's decline against the dollar are seen evaporating on profit taking later in the session, brokers said.

On Tuesday, the 225-share Nikkei average retreated 172.52 points or 0.84 percent to finish at 20,402.74, snapping a three-session winning streak. September Nikkei futures slipped 180 points to close at 20,400.
Brokers expect the Nikkei 225 index to drift between 20,300 and 20,500 on Wednesday.
"The yen fell further, but the polarization of the stock market will probably remain intact," said Kenji Karikomi, deputy general manager at Daiwa Securities Co Ltd.

The yen's recent weakness against the dollar has encouraged buying in export-oriented shares, such as electronics giant Sony Corp. But buying momentum has not spilled over into a wide range of issues amid uncertainty in the country's economic recovery, brokers said.
The dollar was trading at around 118.30 yen in early Asian trade on Wednesday, up from 117.45/50 yen in late Tokyo on Tuesday.
The financial daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun on Wednesday reported that Yamaichi and Daiwa provided a total of 280 million yen to racketeer Ryuichi Koike in illegal deals.
The paper also said that Nikko may have also made illegal deals for Koike, who is a key figure in a high-profile payoff scandal.
